body:
Why India has introduced battery-related programmes

Battery technologies are important for electric mobility, renewable-energy storage, industrial development and energy security. India needs reliable access to the materials, technology and manufacturing capacity used in advanced batteries.

Government initiatives therefore address several connected areas: domestic battery manufacturing, critical-mineral supply, recycling capacity and environmentally responsible management of waste batteries.

The programme details and implementation figures below are presented with their respective official reporting dates. The content cutoff is 14 November 2026.

Production-Linked Incentive Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell Battery Storage

In May 2021, the Union Cabinet approved the Production-Linked Incentive scheme under the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage.

The scheme is administered by the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

Its principal figures are:

  • Approved outlay: ₹18,100 crore.
  • Targeted domestic ACC manufacturing capacity: 50 GWh.
  • Purpose: Encourage domestic manufacturing of advanced battery cells and reduce dependence on imported cells.

An Advanced Chemistry Cell is an advanced electrochemical energy-storage cell. The programme is technology-agnostic within its eligibility framework, meaning it does not require every supported battery to use one identical chemistry.

Understanding reported progress

According to the Ministry of Heavy Industries' 27 March 2026 parliamentary response, 40 GWh of capacity had been awarded to 4 beneficiary firms, while the reported installed capacity was 1 GWh.

These figures must not be confused: awarded capacity represents capacity allocated to beneficiaries under the scheme, whereas installed capacity represents reported manufacturing capacity established.

On 12 November 2026, the ministry reported receiving 22 bids for the remaining 10 GWh capacity offered for grid-scale stationary storage applications. The bids were received under a tender process; receiving bids did not itself mean that the new capacity had already been awarded or installed.

GWh is a unit of energy, not power. In this programme it describes battery-cell manufacturing capacity in energy-storage terms. GW, by contrast, is a unit of power.

Gujarat connection: Jamnagar battery project

The Ministry of Heavy Industries identified a 5 GWh ACC manufacturing project at Jamnagar, Gujarat, under the PLI ACC scheme, associated with Reliance New Energy Battery Storage Ltd.

The project represents a Gujarat connection to India's domestic battery-manufacturing programme. However, the 27 March 2026 ministry report recorded 0 GWh installed capacity for this particular scheme beneficiary at that reporting date.

Thus, a Gujarat project receiving a capacity award should not be described as proof that the awarded manufacturing capacity was already operational.

National Critical Mineral Mission

The Union Cabinet approved the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM) on 29 January 2025.

The mission addresses the security of critical-mineral supplies needed for advanced industries, clean-energy technologies and other important applications.

Its approved financial framework included ₹16,300 crore of proposed expenditure and an additional ₹18,000 crore of expected investment from public-sector undertakings and other stakeholders.

The mission covers important stages of the mineral supply chain, including:

  • Exploration and development of mineral resources.
  • Domestic mining and processing.
  • Access to suitable mineral resources abroad.
  • Recovery of useful minerals from end-of-life products.
  • Development of processing and recycling capabilities.

The mission is therefore broader than lithium mining alone. It concerns multiple critical minerals and the activities needed to make them useful for Indian industries.

Incentive Scheme for Promotion of Critical Mineral Recycling

Under the National Critical Mineral Mission, the Union Cabinet approved a ₹1,500 crore incentive scheme to promote recovery of critical minerals from secondary sources such as battery waste, electronic waste and other suitable scrap materials.

The scheme was approved on 3 September 2025 and notified on 2 October 2025. Its purpose is to encourage domestic recycling capacity and reduce vulnerability to imported raw materials.

A Ministry of Mines update dated 30 April 2026 reported that 58 entities had been approved as eligible for participation. Eligibility approval and proposed capacity should not be treated as evidence that all proposed recycling facilities were already producing recovered materials.

Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022

India's Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change in August 2022, establish a framework for environmentally sound battery-waste management.

The rules cover major battery categories, including portable, automotive, industrial and electric-vehicle batteries.

They are based on Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). Under this approach, producers, including relevant importers, have obligations associated with the collection and recycling or refurbishment of waste batteries placed on the market.

The framework includes a central online EPR mechanism involving producers and eligible recyclers or refurbishers. The rules have been amended since their original notification, so the original 2022 rules must be understood together with applicable amendments.

Government information published on 18 December 2025 stated that the requirement for minimum percentages of domestically recycled materials in new battery manufacturing would apply from FY 2027–28 onwards.

Scheme versus regulation: The ACC PLI programme supports manufacturing capacity. NCMM addresses critical-mineral supply. The critical-mineral recycling incentive encourages recovery capacity. Battery Waste Management Rules establish obligations for managing waste batteries.

Gujarat's wider materials ecosystem

Gujarat's connection to advanced materials is not limited to battery cells. Its industrial base includes ceramics, chemicals, engineering products and other manufacturing activities.

Morbi is an established ceramic-manufacturing cluster, while Jamnagar is a named location for an ACC manufacturing project under the national PLI scheme. These examples represent different parts of the wider materials and manufacturing sector.

As reported in a government update in 2026, critical-mineral processing parks were also being supported in selected states including Gujarat. Such support indicates a planned or developing processing ecosystem, not automatic proof that every associated facility was already operational.

Programme chronology

One-glance revision: Matching the material to its defining property

Competitive-exam questions frequently distinguish material families by the physical property or energy-storage principle involved. The correct classification depends on identifying what the material does, not merely the industry in which it is used.

Prelims focus

  • PLI ACC Battery Storage: approved in May 2021; outlay ₹18,100 crore; target 50 GWh.
  • PLI ACC status reported on 27 March 2026: 40 GWh awarded and 1 GWh installed.
  • On 12 November 2026, the Ministry of Heavy Industries reported 22 bids for 10 GWh of grid-scale storage capacity.
  • Jamnagar, Gujarat: 5 GWh ACC capacity award under the PLI scheme; not reported as installed in the March 2026 statement.
  • National Critical Mineral Mission: approved on 29 January 2025.
  • Battery Waste Management Rules: 2022; based on Extended Producer Responsibility.
  • Trap: A manufacturing target, a capacity award, an investment proposal and installed operational capacity are different measures.
